In 1618, angry noblemen threw two government officials out of a castle window in Prague!
They fell more than fifteen meters. And they survived, because they landed in a giant pile of manure!
But this stinky escape lit the fuse of the Thirty Years' War, one of the deadliest wars in European history!
It began with religion. Bohemia was mostly Protestant, but its new king was a devout Catholic, who kept taking away their rights.
So on the twenty-third of May, a furious crowd marched to Prague Castle, and demanded answers.
The shouting got louder. And louder. Then the nobles grabbed two officials, and their secretary, and hurled them straight out of the window!
The Catholics said angels caught the men. The Protestants said they landed in a heap of horse dung.
One of them, the secretary, was later rewarded with a noble title: Philip von Hohenfall, which means, of the high fall!
But the emperor was not amused. Armies marched in, and neighbor after neighbor joined the fight.
The war spread across Europe for thirty years. Villages burned, famine and plague followed, and millions died.
Some regions of Germany lost a third of their people, or more.
All because a few men took a short flight, and landed in a very soft place!
So if you like history, where one pile of manure changes the world, follow for more stories like this!
